Few careers hold my attention like mechanical engineering, especially the challenge of turning ideas into practical systems that improve everyday life. Ever since I was young, I have been fascinated by how machines work, and that curiosity grew into a clear commitment to building solutions that are efficient, reliable, and made to last. It is for this reason that I am certain of my desire to continue developing as a Mechanical Engineer. I am originally from Nigeria, and I hold a Master’s degree from a university ranked in the global top 500. Across my academic and project work, I have completed 7 projects with tangible outcomes, each reinforcing my interest in translating complex mechanical problems into designs that work not only in theory but also in production and use. One example came when I needed to use a new engineering tool for a project; within a few weeks I was using it confidently, and soon afterwards I was helping teammates set up their first models and avoid the early mistakes I had already worked through.

My experience has also shown me how much I value solving difficult technical problems in ways that can be applied beyond a single task. In one project, I developed an original solution to a mechanical design problem that others had not managed to resolve, and the approach was later taken up outside my own team for similar work. On another occasion, colleagues began coming to me with questions in my own area, asking me to review calculations or talk through design choices before they moved ahead. Beyond the technical side, one of my favourite memories was taking my family to a science and engineering exhibition where they saw a prototype I had helped develop and immediately started asking questions about every moving part. Hearing a younger relative proudly tell strangers, “They build things that actually work!” made this career feel especially meaningful. I am now eager to bring my training, practical mindset, and enthusiasm to a Mechanical Engineer role where I can contribute dependable solutions and continue growing through real engineering challenges.

What first drew me to carpentry was that blend of creativity and hands-on problem-solving: the chance to build spaces and furniture that become part of people’s daily lives. I hold a Doctorate from a university ranked in the global top 100, and across my studies and applied work I completed 5 projects with tangible outcomes. That experience taught me how to approach work methodically and carry ideas through to a finished result. When I needed to use a new digital design and planning tool that was unfamiliar to me, I built confidence with it gradually over more than a year of steady use, until it became part of how I prepared and checked work. In one team setting, repeated delays were being caused by measurements and material adjustments not lining up smoothly on site, so I introduced a simple step-by-step checking sheet that helped us catch issues earlier and keep the job moving.

I also value the practical exchange of knowledge that good work depends on. In my own area, colleagues have sometimes come to me with questions about planning details and fit, and I have enjoyed talking through options with them clearly and directly. Combined with my interest in reading a space carefully, measuring accurately, and producing clean, durable work, these experiences have confirmed the kind of Carpenter I want to be: someone who contributes reliable workmanship, thoughtful solutions, and genuine pride in what is built.

I have always been drawn to the way libraries open doors for people, whether they are searching for knowledge, comfort, or a fresh start, and that belief led me toward a career built on connecting communities with information. Originally from Peru, I hold a Bachelor’s degree from a university not listed in the major global rankings, and my academic path gave me a grounded appreciation for how access to clear, reliable information can shape opportunity. That foundation strengthened my commitment to librarianship and to the public service at its heart.

What continues to hold my attention most is the work of turning large amounts of information into guidance that feels manageable and useful for the person in front of me, whether that means helping someone begin with a simple question or supporting more detailed research. Over more than a year of steady practice, I became comfortable using a new digital cataloguing and resource-management tool that was unfamiliar to me at first, and that gradual process showed me how sustained learning improves the support I can offer. In one role, our team kept losing time to a recurring issue with inconsistent resource records, so I put together a simple shared checking process that reduced repeated corrections and helped daily work move more smoothly. Colleagues now sometimes come to me with questions in my own area, particularly when they need help locating the right source quickly or organizing information in a clearer way.

Alongside my degree, I completed 2 projects with tangible outcomes, both of which reinforced the value of careful research, organization, and follow-through. In addition, these experiences have helped me build independence, teamwork, and calm decision-making under pressure. I consider myself thoughtful, dependable, and committed to service. Looking ahead, I am eager to continue developing as a Librarian and to contribute with care, clarity, and purpose in a role that helps people discover what they need.
